provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Each object is an L-tromino: three cells of a 2x2 box with one corner (the gap) empty. The elbow is the cell diagonally opposite the gap, and the vector from elbow to gap is a diagonal unit step. An object of original colour 5 gets a copy in original colour 4, shifted one step along that diagonal (toward the gap). An object of original colour 2 gets a copy in original colour 3, shifted one step against it (away from the gap). Copies paint only background cells that lie inside the grid. All 5-derived shadows are stamped first and all 2-derived shadows afterwards, so colour 3 wins where shadows overlap. This matches the generator's draw order. The direction is defined relative to each object's own gap and elbow. Any rotation or reflection moves the gap, the elbow and the shift together, so the visible-coordinate rule is the same for every d4 and needs no axis-specific rewrite. The factory therefore only bakes palette constants into the program: background palette[7], source colours palette[5] and palette[2], and shadow colours palette[4] and palette[3]. Objects are found as 4-connected single-colour components.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the palette is a bijection, so the five role colours stay distinct. Assumes the constructor's spacing guarantee: boxes are kept at least one cell apart, so a shadow never lands on another object. If that guarantee failed, the generator's overwrite order could differ from this background-only painting. Components that are not 3-cell L shapes inside a 2x2 box are ignored. The d4 argument is deliberately unused, because the mechanism is invariant under D4. No fixture contradictions were found. I have not run any tests.
